doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Time at Wilberforce and being drafted
summary: He explains his time at Wilberforce, clarifies he was drafted rather than enlisting, and recalls his romantic wish to be a Marine.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: How long were you at Wilberforce?

They called me up – the Army called me up. I was nearing 18. I was at Wilberforce once, and then I left, worked for six months, got myself together, and went back to Wilberforce, and then I was there for two years, not exactly going to school, because Wilberforce was a place that attracted people from Cincinnati, gangsters. Most of the guys at Wilberforce were studying business. They took the business course. Later on, most of them became slicks.

Hustlers. You said something interesting. One of the conflicting things I’ve heard was that your tuberculosis – I’ll tell you two things I’ve heard. One was that your tuberculosis was discovered on a physical when you tried to enlist in the Army, and the other was that it was picked up, diagnosed in a physical, when you were drafted. Now you just said you were called up. Does that mean you were drafted?
Okay. So that clears that up. You didn’t enlist.
Again I wish we had a camera.
In a way it’s true. I enlisted romantically to become a Marine from purely ridiculous reasons, purely ridiculous.
The macho. Are we back to the girls again, kissing the girls and all of that good stuff?
I understand. Be all you can be, huh?
